scamsFlagged.note: A ceiling: we wrote these cases

scamsFlagged.label: Blind scenarios, simulated customer (seed 17)
scamsFlagged.note: 40 fresh cases, after the 'after asking' rule

findings.found: A supplier 'emailed us' the details and the reader counted that as the customer checking independently.
findings.fix: The reader is now told that details received by email, text or message are not independent checking.

findings.found: A coached customer said the payee was 'recommended by a trusted contact', and the guard counted that referral as proof.
findings.fix: Not changed. A recommendation cannot be checked, and tuning against one case would be guesswork. Recorded as a known limit.

findings.found: Coached victims still passed after the guard asked: their replies were calm reassurance with nothing concrete ('everything is fine, push it through').
findings.fix: After asking, a new payee that nothing backs up now adds risk, and empty reassurance or pushing to hurry counts as evasive.
findings.status: Improved: coached victims 0 of 5, then 2, then 4 of 5 on fresh seeds

findings.found: Blind scenarios: every coached victim with a bland note on an ordinary payment was allowed (0 of 5).
findings.fix: Ask when a new payee is still unexplained after reading the note. Payee reputation from other banks is the stronger defence and is not modelled.

findings.found: Coached victims still passed when the note only claimed a reason ('family expenses', 'legal fees').
findings.fix: A claim is not proof. For a new payee the guard now asks unless the customer met them, was introduced by someone, or checked independently.

findings.found: Our fix for business owners went too far: a $16,557 scam (5 times their usual payment) scored only 30 points.
findings.fix: The scenario factory caught it. The allowance for business customers was softened from double to one and a half times.

findings.found: Blind test: scams with tiny notes and small amounts slipped through (4 of 25).
findings.fix: Ask the customer a short question when the evidence is thin, then decide again.

findings.found: A surprise gift ('keep it secret') was treated as concealment and held.
findings.fix: The reader now tells a harmless surprise from real concealment, and the guard asks before it holds.

findings.found: Small-business owners got friction on 43% of normal payments.
findings.fix: Larger payments count for less against a business customer's own habits, by half as much again.

findings.found: Eight payments to one new payee in a day only ever earned a question.
findings.fix: 15 days of history: repeat payments to a new payee, total sent to one payee, and heavy spend all add risk.

findings.found: Hidden orders to the checker, in eight wordings including other languages.
findings.fix: Orders are treated as a warning sign. All eight were held on the first run.

findings.found: A second test file was built from templates: 17 unique notes in 50 cases.
findings.fix: Rejected as a headline test. Replaced by an automatic scenario factory with a simulated customer.

findings.found: Cloud Run swallows the /healthz path, so the health check returned 404.
findings.fix: The tester checks the home page, and the server's own route moved to /api/health.

findings.found: Every answer reveals the risk score and reasons, which could help an attacker tune a message.
findings.fix: Kept for the demo. A production version would send only the action and a warning to the customer.

findings.found: We tried to learn from real complaint stories published by a US regulator. Its public API returns no story text.
findings.fix: Dropped. We use regulator statistics for realism and our own scenario factory for testing.

limits: A customer coached to be bland can still get a scam through when nothing else about the payment is unusual. This is the hardest case.
A believable referral ('recommended by a trusted contact') can still lower the risk, and nobody can check it.
All data is made up. Nothing here has met real customers or real fraud.
Our own 99% is a ceiling, because we wrote the cases. The blind test is the fairer guide.
Some quiet scams show nothing unusual in the payment itself. Only the customer's words can reveal them, and a coached customer can hide them.
Payee reputation (for example accounts reported by other banks) is not modelled. A real bank would add it.
The prototype runs on the free trial's allowance, with rate limits and a cost guard, so it is not sized for heavy traffic.

scenarioRun.title: Blind scenarios, by kind (seed 17, 40 scenarios)
scenarioRun.overall: 38 of 40 as expected. Earlier runs on other seeds: 19 of 24, then 36, then 37 of 40
